lead: Mobile plumbing deals with heavy rain, hurricanes, humidity and historic homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Mobile.
risk: storm flooding and backups, aging pipes in historic homes and root-filled sewer lines
risk_short: flooding, old pipes and sewer roots
why: Oakleigh, De Tonti Square and Midtown have homes from the 1830s to the 1930s, many on raised foundations with galvanized supply lines and clay or cast-iron drains. Live oaks send roots into old sewer lines.
Mobile is one of the rainiest cities in the U.S., and hurricanes bring surge and long outages. Heavy rain backs up drains in low areas.
utility: Mobile Area Water and Sewer System (MAWSS)
water: MAWSS treats water mainly from Big Creek Lake. It is soft.
tips: Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Check historic district rules before exterior work.
areas: PipeMend works in the Oakleigh Garden District, De Tonti Square, Midtown, Spring Hill, West Mobile, Crichton and every other Mobile neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Mobile permitting office (Build Mobile), and plumbers must be licensed by the Alabama Plumbers and Gas Fitters Examining Board.

faq.q: Why do Mobile drains back up in storms?
faq.a: Mobile gets some of the heaviest rain in the country, and low streets drain slowly. Heavy rain can fill sewers and push water back through floor drains. A backwater valve helps.
